MEASUREMENT (pure-math script, no model import): for all 169 single fire offsets in a 13x13 window and 20000 random fire sets, `own OR 4-adjacent OR manhattan<=1` == `manhattan<=1` and `own OR 4-adjacent OR manhattan<=3` == `manhattan<=3` with 0 mismatches; diamond sizes r=1:5 cells, r=2:13, r=3:25.
claims.detail: FULL STATE TABLE at HEAD. (1) pos None -> no range: advance() returns at 1614-1615 and the trigger itself returns False at 1865-1866. (2) dead -> same, no range. (3) exiting True -> trigger returns False: NO retreat range at all while carrying a victim; the exiting branch (1711-1746) only uses _move_toward's per-neighbour hazard tiers (burning neighbour cells hard-excluded 2287-2288; adjacent-fire/smoke soft tiers 2314-2327), which is path scoring of the 4 candidate cells, not a distance trigger, and the route-blocked BFS is skipped when exiting (2280). (4) idle (target_pos falsy, not exiting) -> own-cell fire OR own-cell smoke OR fire at Manhattan <= idle_buffer (3 at shipped defaults). (5) has target_pos, not exiting -> own-cell fire OR own-cell smoke OR fire at Manhattan <= 1. SELECTOR is `self.target_pos` TRUTHINESS (1871), NOT `assigned`; `assigned` is never consulted by the trigger. In production code the two cannot disagree: all four model writer sites set/clear them together and the only lone write (agents.py:1611) replaces one truthy cell with another; (0,0) is a non-empty tuple so still truthy. They CAN disagree only in synthetic setups (tests write .target_pos directly, 36 occurrences across 10 test files). ADJACENCY: _cell_adjacent_to_fire is 4-neighbour, so 'adjacent OR manhattan<=1' is exactly the manhattan<=1 diamond (5 cells) and the adjacency test is redundant with the distance test in both branches (verified by measurement). SMOKE: yes - own-cell active smoke (and own-cell fire) returns True BEFORE any distance test and regardless of state, so the trigger is NOT purely a distance-to-fire test; smoke is per-cell Fire state (agents.py:1816-1831) and can be active with no burning cell inside the diamond. WHY 'modified': (a) 'only' holds at SHIPPED DEFAULTS only - with the fire mechanic armed there are further unit-centred Manhattan reaches (extinguish 2, firebreak 1) and the idle radius becomes T in {1,2} on engaged steps (see C5); (b) the constant 3 has a second reader, _idle_needs_survival_move (1883-1897), and a complement, _cell_is_ideal_idle_standoff (>= 4) - on the unit's CURRENT cell the latter is exactly NOT(idle trigger), i.e. the same 3|4 boundary, not a new radius; (c) the assigned radius 1 is a BARE LITERAL at agents.py:1879 with no named constant. Old doc refs 1696-1704 are stale.

FIREBREAK: unit-centred Manhattan reach 1 (own cell or a 4-neighbour) onto a band cell; the BAND itself is FIRE-centred, not unit-centred - ignitable cells whose EUCLIDEAN distance to the nearest burning cell is in (2, 5] (squared 4 < d2 <= 25). ENGAGED_RETREAT_RANGE: idle retreat distance T = K for K in {1,2}, only on a step where a plan exists AND the unit is not suspended AND the exit guard holds (2436-2439, 2461); anything else (3, 0, negatives, junk, >3) -> the full buffer 3. 'standable' cells are those outside Manhattan T of every burning cell and smoke-free (2585-2599) - again fire-centred. MISSION_GATE: purely TEMPORAL (engage only once every managed victim is rescued or dead, 2481-2490); it adds no range. LIVE AT SHIPPED DEFAULTS? NO. With EXTINGUISH=0 and FIREBREAK=0, _firefight_prepare returns None at 2378-2379 before reading the mission gate, suppression or dry-run; therefore `firefight is None`, idle_buffer == IDLE_RETREAT_SAFETY_BUFFER == 3 on every step (1625-1627), _firefight_execute / _firefight_after_retreat / _firefight_log_row are never reached (1665, 1668 are `if firefight is not None`). Additionally, ENGAGED_RETREAT_RANGE=3 alone would keep T=3 even with FIREBREAK=1, and would disable EXTINGUISH outright (3 < 2 is False at 2393). idle_buffer can differ from 3 only if (EXTINGUISH or FIREBREAK) AND K in {1,2} AND mission resolved (gate=1) AND a plan exists AND not suspended AND exit guard true.

claims.detail: PER CONSTANT. IDLE_RETREAT_MAX_CELLS=6: a Manhattan LEASH measured from `_idle_retreat_origin` (the cell where the current retreat manoeuvre began) plus a STEP-COUNT cap; NOT centred on the unit's current cell (it coincides with it only at the instant of (re-)anchoring, agents.py:1963-1967). Also reused as a leash around the absence EXIT cell for re-entry. _cell_is_ideal_idle_standoff (>= 4): a predicate on an arbitrary CELL (candidate neighbours at 2076, the landing cell at 2038, the current cell at 1940/2428); it is the retreat's stopping condition. Evaluated on the unit's current cell it is exactly NOT(idle trigger) - the same 3|4 boundary as C3, not an additional radius. SECURITY_DISTANCE=10: UAV-to-UAV EUCLIDEAN spacing (collision metric MR2) and UAV team spread for the comm-relay test; never touches a firefighter. STANDOFF_*: fire-tracker UAV standoff scoring against fire, UAV-centred; never touches a firefighter. FF_RESCUE_ABSENCE_MIN/MAX_STEPS: DURATIONS in steps for the off-grid hand-over, not cells. ADDITIONAL TRAPS found at HEAD: `self.radius = 3` at agents.py:29 is the FIRE agent's spread neighbourhood (used at agents.py:61,74), not a firefighter attribute; VICTIM_FLEE_TRIGGER_DISTANCE=3 / VICTIM_FLEE_MAX_DISPLACEMENT=6 (cfv:142-143) are victim-centred and deliberately borrow the numerals 3 and 6 (cfv:130-134); `_VICTIM_HAZARD_BUFFER = 2` (uav_executor.py:49) is UAV-side; FIREFIGHT_BAND_INNER_SQ/OUTER_SQ (agents.py:1478-1479) are centred on BURNING cells, euclidean, and dark by default; FIREFIGHT_EXTINGUISH_REACH=2 / FIREFIGHT_FIREBREAK_REACH=1 ARE unit-centred Manhattan but dark by default (C5); _firefighter_fire_enclosed (wildfire_model.py:3886-3898) is a 4-neighbour all-burning test, not a range.

claims.detail: TODAY fr.firefighters carries ONLY id/x/y/color - dead is recoverable from color (#000000), off-grid from absence. It carries NO target_pos, NO exiting, NO assigned. The en-route state is only indirectly inferable by matching a marker's (x,y) to an assignment's (fx,fy); idle vs EXITING is NOT distinguishable from the frame payload at all (neither has an assignment line), yet they differ in the model (idle: radius 3; exiting: no range). A state-dependent frame needs per unit: (1) has_target = bool(target_pos) - the model's actual selector (agents.py:1871); `assigned` is a safe proxy in production (C3) but is not what the code tests; (2) exiting; (3) dead (have, via color/alive) and pos None (have, via omission). `status` is NOT a usable selector: it is "en_route" at assign (wildfire_model.py:4559), becomes "assigned" when a route block clears (agents.py:2355), stays unchanged when `exiting` flips (agents.py:1675 sets only exiting/exit_target), and is "route_blocked" while still targeted. RADII: 3 can be read from agents.IDLE_RETREAT_SAFETY_BUFFER and sent once on /start like fov_radius/victim_flee_radius (serve_dashboard.py:433-442); 1 has NO symbol (bare literal, agents.py:1879) and would have to be hard-coded. If the fire mechanic is ever armed with K in {1,2}, the idle radius becomes a per-STEP value T that exists only in movement_reason key_factors (`retreat_distance=ctx["T"]`, agents.py:2776) and _firefight_log rows (agents.py:2817) - in no dashboard payload. ID MISMATCH: fr.firefighters ids are mesa unique_ids while panel.firefighter_view ids are 'ff_unit_i', so the browser cannot join the two by id; the state fields would have to be added to fr.firefighters in _capture_frame directly (cheapest: read target_pos/exiting off the agent at serve_dashboard.py:195-205, where both are already being read for the assignment line).

TIMING CAVEAT FOR ANY FRAME: the scheduler is mesa SimultaneousActivation (wildfire_model.py:180) and Fire agents advance before firefighters (agents.py:127-131 comment: `the schedule advances every Fire agent (unique ids 0..N-1, added first in reset()) before any firefighter`). _capture_frame runs after the step, so a frame drawn at frame t shows unit position t against fire t, but the trigger the unit evaluates next is against fire t+1. 'Fire inside the diamond' at frame t predicts a retreat next step; 'fire outside' does not guarantee none.

SMOKE MAKES THE TRIGGER NON-GEOMETRIC: own-cell active smoke returns True before any distance test in every non-exiting state (agents.py:1868-1869), and the same clause is in _idle_needs_survival_move (1895) and _cell_meets_required_idle_safety (1914-1915). Smoke is per-cell state that outlives burning (Smoke.smoke_step, agents.py:195-200; Fire.step keeps calling it at agents.py:114-115). A diamond frame is therefore a sufficient-not-necessary picture of the retreat rule: a unit can retreat with no burning cell inside it.

IF THE FEATURE IS EVER ARMED the 'state-dependent' table grows a third and fourth case: idle+engaged (T=K in {1,2}) and idle+suspended (`_firefight_suspended` latched on ANY retreat while K<3, agents.py:2797-2799; cleared only on an ideal standoff, 2428-2430) which forces T back to 3. Neither `_firefight_suspended` nor T is published anywhere. At shipped defaults none of this exists (C5).
